claims.text: DenseNet connects every layer to every other layer in a feed-forward manner
claims.reason: The paper abstract states DenseNet 'connects each layer to every other layer in a feed-forward fashion'.

claims.text: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 contain 32×32 pixel natural images
claims.reason: Section 4.1 states 'The two CIFAR datasets consist of colored natural images with 32×32 pixels'.

claims.text: ImageNet (ILSVRC 2012) contains 1.2 million images across 1,000 classes
claims.reason: Section 4.1 states 'The ILSVRC 2012 classification dataset consists 1.2 million images for training... from 1,000 classes'.

claims.text: Models were trained for 60 to 400 epochs on CIFAR and SVHN
claims.reason: Section 4.2 states CIFAR was trained for 300 epochs and SVHN for 40 epochs; the range '60 to 400' does not appear anywhere in the paper.

claims.text: ImageNet models were trained for 90 epochs
claims.reason: Section 4.2 explicitly states 'On ImageNet, we train models for 90 epochs'.

claims.text: Initial learning rate of 0.1, decayed by a factor of 10 at specific intervals
claims.reason: Section 4.2 states 'The initial learning rate is set to 0.1, and is divided by 10 at 50% and 75% of the total number of training epochs'.

claims.text: Weight decay of 10^-4 and Nesterov momentum of 0.9 were used
claims.reason: Section 4.2 states 'we use a weight decay of 10^-4 and a Nesterov momentum of 0.9 without dampening'.

claims.text: Transition layers consist of a 1×1 convolution and a 2×2 average pooling layer
claims.reason: Section 3 (Pooling layers) states transition layers consist of 'a batch normalization layer and an 1×1 convolutional layer followed by a 2×2 average pooling layer'.

claims.text: Growth rate k determines how many new feature maps each layer contributes to the global state
claims.reason: Section 3 states 'The growth rate regulates how much new information each layer contributes to the global state'.

claims.text: Bottleneck layers (1×1 convolutions) are introduced in the DenseNet-BC variant to improve computational efficiency
claims.reason: The paper defines DenseNet-B as the bottleneck-only variant and DenseNet-BC as the combination of both bottleneck and compression (theta<1 at transition layers); the summary incorrectly conflates bottleneck layers with the DenseNet-BC label.

claims.text: DenseNet was evaluated against ResNets, FractalNets, and Highway Networks
claims.reason: Table 2 and Section 4.3 compare DenseNets against ResNet, FractalNet, and Highway Network baselines.

claims.text: DenseNets achieve comparable or superior accuracy with substantially fewer parameters
claims.reason: Section 5 states 'DenseNet-BC only requires around 1/3 of the parameters of ResNets' to achieve comparable accuracy, consistent with the summary's claim.

claims.text: DenseNet-BC with L=100 and k=12 achieves comparable performance to the 1001-layer pre-activation ResNet using 90% fewer parameters
claims.reason: Section 4.3 explicitly states DenseNet-BC (L=100, k=12) achieves 'comparable performance... as the 1001-layer pre-activation ResNet using 90% fewer parameters'.
